chainGuard.detail: block.chainid is referenced exactly once, at DeployMocks.s.sol:365, inside a console.log. There is NO require(block.chainid == 31337). The repo's own CLAUDE.md ('Configuration Safety', rule 5) mandates that anvil relaxations 'must be gated behind an explicit block.chainid == 31337 branch and clearly commented — never share an unsafe default code path between local and real networks'. This script is composed almost entirely of such relaxations (permissionless mock mints, amountMin=0 liquidity adds, deployer-as-phUSD-minter, the default anvil key from ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY), yet nothing structurally prevents it being pointed at another RPC. The only '31337' is a hardcoded STRING in the emitted progress JSON (:2311) and in the output filename (:2334), which would silently MISLABEL a non-anvil run. Contrast script/interactions/AddressLoader.sol, which in this very delta ADDED exactly such a require with the rationale 'on mainnet that is an approve/transfer to a stranger's contract'.

hazards.title: A local anvil run rewrites the mainnet address book's compile-time type guard
hazards.detail: server/deployments/mainnet-addresses.ts imports ContractAddresses from ./addresses and annotates `mainnetAddresses: ContractAddresses`. addresses.ts is regenerated on EVERY local anvil run from anvil's local.json. So `npm run dev` rewrites the type contract the hand-maintained MAINNET address file is validated against. A contract present on mainnet but not _trackDeployment'ed in DeployMocks vanishes from the interface, silently un-typing the mainnet key; a purely local mock added to DeployMocks becomes a REQUIRED key on the mainnet object. The DROPPED_CONTRACT_NAMES / UNISWAP_V2_BACKING_NAMES denylists in extract-addresses.js exist solely to hold this line, and only a code comment enforces the lockstep. Story 078 states the rule outright: 'hand-deleting a key from addresses.ts is not durable — the next local anvil deploy regenerates it'.

promotionReadyMirror.verdict: `dev` mirrors the promotion-ready cutover's END STATE well and its CUTOVER MECHANICS poorly. Everything that is a greenfield deploy-and-wire (a, c, g, h) is faithfully reproduced, and the staker migration (d) and PhlimboV3 migration (g) are genuine rehearsals that already fed corrections back into the mainnet plan. But every behaviour that is specifically about REPLACING a live contract — replaceDispatcher (b), hook repointing (f), old-minter retirement (e), pot rescue (a-gap), BPT custody + baselines (k) — is absent, because the local chain has no incumbent to replace. The claim 'the dev chain rehearses the whole sequence of mainnet cutovers locally' is therefore true for the destination and false for the transition.
